rationale: verdict stands. with a $\operatorname{Re} \operatorname{Tr} U^2$ term Sigma(648) matches SU(3) at the $N_t = 4$ transition (chi(2, 2) 0.375 against 0.378, chi(3, 3) 0.262 against 0.278), and on the trajectories measured its spacing stops shrinking there. No finite subgroup of SU(3) contains Sigma(648) properly, so any gate outside it generates a dense subgroup, a theorem (L5), and the fear beat with Sigma(648) on each role generates all of su(9) (E-QTM-0118). But the steps come slowly: the first word closer to the qutrit T gate than any classical element needs 4 fear beats, 0.362 against 0.395 (E-QTM-0104)
